tests: presence is not resolvability: the four shapes that used to PASS are each named

consumesExternalOutput.program: the built tiphys CLI of a staged install: `node <install>/dist/bin/tiphys.js doctor --for full`
consumesExternalOutput.provenance: The two halves of the resolvability predicate, mutated one at a time. Member 0 defangs the CONSUMER FILTER, so a directory carrying one unrelated file, a directory carrying only a subdirectory and a directory whose members are all zero bytes all resolve again. Member 1 defangs the CONTENT FLOOR by one comparison, so a zero-byte member and a zero-byte AGENTS.md resolve again. The cited capture is the output of the program this behaviour reports through, taken 2026-08-15 on node v26.6.0 against a real staged install of this head, one fresh copy per shape, with a stub gh on PATH and a remote configured so that kernel-artifacts is the only check able to drive the exit code. It records all four shapes as FAIL with exit 1; the E1.7 hazard review measured the same four as PASS with FAIL count zero against round 0.
